item.title: Labuschagne's form hits record low but Australia hint at future
item.description: Marnus Labuschagne has not scored a Test century since the 2023 Ashes [Getty Images] Third Test, Cape Town (day two of five) South Africa 329: Ackerman 95; Starc 6-72 Australia 330-4: Inglis 85*; Jansen 2-37 Australia lead by one run Scorecard Marnus Labuschagne has been front and centre for an era of Australian cricket. Chirping, chewing and, with bat in hand, often appearing to idolise and mimic his team-mate Steve Smith. Smith has been ruled out of the enthralling decisive Test against South Africa with a neck injury. Without him, Australia wanted their number three to feast at last chance saloon, where he has been perched for an eternity, on day two in Cape Town. The 32-year-old lasted five deliveries and did not score a run. Labuschagne failed to scored a Test century for the 48th time in a row - a new record for the number of innings an Australian top order batter has waited to raise his bat at three figures. "That will never be broken," said former Australia quick Jason Gillespie on ABC. "I say that because, respectfully, I don't think anyone will be given that length of time again." There was a time when, from his insertion into the 2019 Ashes as a concussion substitute until the end of England's next quest to win back the earn, Labuschagne averaged 65 in Test cricket. Repeat that over a Test career and only Sir Donald Bradman's mark of 99.94 would be ahead. Instead, since his last Test century at Old Trafford in 2023, he averages 24.77. Labuschagne may get one more chance in this Test, should Australia not progress from their position of 330-4, leading by one run, and dismiss South Africa before needing to pad up again. Even that may not be enough. "I just feel it is too far gone now," Gillespie added. "It is a very big sample size. Australia are at a point where they need to look elsewhere." Labuschagne's technique has been poured over again and again as his slump progressed. In August, the great Ricky Ponting, one of his predecessors as Australia's number three, called for the axe to fall. "He can't score off the back foot," was Ponting's cutting remark. Having batted nicely in three or four innings in this series only to give it away after reaching 30, here he was stuck on the crease, playing back to a full ball and nicking spinner Simon Harmer to slip. "That's nerves and the pressure the selectors have put him under for an extended period of time," said former Australia batter Simon Katich on SEN Radio. "They put him in this position by not making the decision to give him a breather." It felt like all of Labuschagne's issues collapsing into one. But if his pained stare down the pitch signalled the end of something, what followed hinted at their future. With Travis Head already out and Labuschagne following, the score 58-2 in reply to the Proteas' 329, there was no Smith to steer Australia out of this tricky spot. item.title: Commanders make several key roster moves coming out of bye week
item.description: Johnny Newton suffered a torn pectoral muscle in the first Commanders preseason game. That’s normally a season-ender. It’s not the case this time. The second-year defensive lineman had his 21-day practice window opened on Wednesday, formally designating him to return off injured reserve. By rule , Newton must be activated within that window or he’ll be held on season-ending injured reserve. “He has worked his ass off,” head coach Dan Quinn said. Getting Newton back would be important for the team, considering his talents as an interior pass rusher and a stout run defender. That wasn’t the only roster move Washington made on Wednesday afternoon. The Commanders formally placed receiver Terry McLaurin on injured reserve. He suffered a season-ending torn patellar tendon during a Week 6 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Van Jefferson was promoted off the practice squad in a corresponding move. Jefferson was chosen over Jaden Bradley, and provides a more veteran presences in terms of depth. We have made the following roster moves: – Placed WR Terry McLaurin on the Reserve/Injured List – Signed WR Van Jefferson from the practice squad – Signed OLB Kyle Kennard to the practice squad pic.twitter.com/WvIWPHFx9g — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) October 28, 2026 He joins a six-man group that has dealt with some significant injuries. Expect Treylon Burks to man the X position and to have Antonio Williams significantly increase his snap count.

item.title: Saracens did unbelievable job with Auvaa - Lam
item.description: Forward Auvaa has been signed by Bristol after being let go by Saracens this month [Shutterstock] Saracens did everything they could for Samoan forward Totoa Auvaa before sacking him, according to his new director of rugby at Bristol Bears. Auvaa, 21, was involved in a nightclub altercation with England cricketers Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson in June, though Sarries stood by him at the time. He was, however, sacked two weeks ago following another late-night incident in St Albans, which police are investigating. When Auvaa's signing was announced on Monday , Bristol boss Pat Lam said he believed in giving people second chances. On Wednesday he told BBC Radio Bristol: "People make mistakes. I felt he will fit in well here. "He's training this week and looks very impressive. There's no doubt that we believe he's someone that has ability to grow and develop as a really outstanding rugby player." Lam revealed that England, British & Irish Lions and Saracens captain Maro Itoje had checked in on Auvaa this week as he started life with the Bears. Lam said: "Saracens did an unbelievable job, they gave him the opportunity, they got him an English teacher, Maro itoje has been like a mentor to him. "Maro got hold of him yesterday to check in and see how he's doing. They did as well as they could, the decision they made they felt was right and I understand that. "I was asked if I would give him another opportunity and I am happy to do it." Lam hopes he can be a positive influence on his fellow Samoan and said Auvaa had not been issued with any ultimatums about his future behaviour. He said: "We highlight what we expect. Every player has some sort of past but the past is in the past and you have got to learn. "My whole thing in life, with five kids at nearly 60, I look back and go, there were lots of ups and downs, but I am who I am because of the experiences I went through and then having the right people. "Some of the decisions I made, rugby influenced a lot of it and people who mentored me and took me under their wing shaped me this way. "I have benefited from it. There's a lot of stories that could go this way or the other way. The beauty of our great game is every good team has a good environment. "We're all human, there's no guarantees, you're always going to be criticised for anything and praised for different things, you just have to keep pushing through. "This is human nature. It depends who's giving you the opportunity. I see him no different to lots of people on this earth that have made mistakes." Auvaa made one senior appearance for Saracens, playing 20 minutes of a Prem Rugby Cup match in September. But Lam hinted that he might match that number for Bears very soon with two group games to come in the competition against Sale and Bath in November. Lam added: "He'll look to feature in the Prem Cup. He's got to learn all of our systems and our ways. He's made a good start. It's about how quickly you can learn." item.title: Colt Nichols moves to PRMX Yamaha Partzilla, his fifth team in five seasons
item.description: Colt Nichols will move from the Twisted Tea Suzuki team to Team ROKiT Partzilla PRMX Yamaha for the 2027 season. Nichols finished 15th in the Monster Energy Supercross 450 division and was 16th in the SuperMotocross World Championship playoffs. Casey Cochran signs with Yamaha Star Racing for 2027 SuperMotocross Casey Cochran was the final piece of the 250 puzzle after Factory Husqvarna’s departure from the SuperMotocross League. Dan Beaver , The highlight of his career came in 2021 when he won the 250 SX East divisional championship, but that was a pyrrhic victory. Having raced on the Yamaha Star Racing team since 2016, he was forced to move up to the 450 division per Supercross rules and there was no room for him in Yamaha's premiere team. "I’ve been talking to the team and working with Julien [Perrier] for several months and I’m happy we have been able to put a deal together that gets me back on a Yamaha where I’ve had a lot of success," Nichols said. "I’m happy to be back on the Yamaha and this new YZ450 feels like home already." From 2023 through 2026, Nichols competed for four organizations, often switching teams mid-season: Team Honda (2023 Supercross), Rick Ware Racing (2023 Motocross and SuperMotocross), the Factory Beta team (2024 Supercross), and the Twisted Tea Suzuki team (2024-2026). The 2023 Honda deal came about when the team and Ken Roczen parted ways. Now back on a Yamaha, he hopes to rekindle the magic from his 250 days. "We are excited to have a rider of Colt’s caliber and we think he will fit right in with the team," said team owner Julien Perrier. Nichols will continue top run his iconic No. 45, keeping his nickname of Colt 45 alive.

item.title: Fede Valverde is injury-free and will be available on Sunday
item.description: Fede Valverde is injury-free and will be available on Sunday Good news for Real Madrid. Federico Valverde, the team captain, has no injury and will be available for the next league match against Racing de Santander. Medical tests carried out on Wednesday ruled out any significant muscle injury for the Uruguayan, who had to be substituted in the second half of last Sunday's El Clásico. This means José Mourinho can name him in the starting lineup next weekend. Mourinho has found the perfect balance with a masterstroke: playing Valverde at right-back. This tactical tweak makes room for Arda Güler to add creativity and control in midfield, while the Uruguayan holds down the flank with his formidable physical power. The coaching staff are closely monitoring his adaptation to a role that has completely transformed the team's defensive solidity. item.title: Set Point #10: Eyes on the postseason
item.description: Another 0-2 week has come and gone for Northwestern, bringing its record to 7-14 on the year and 0-10 in Big Ten play. The Wildcats lost in three sets to Michigan on Oct. 22 and then were swept by Purdue on Sunday, falling 150-110 in the two matches. Bella Bullington and Mara Štiglic led the team in kills across the two games, totaling 20 and 16, respectively, but it was yet another disappointing showing. The two additional results emphasize a trend of the season: simply put, the ‘Cats are not operating at the same level, in any regard, as the other Big Ten teams. Across its 10 conference games, NU has won four of the 34 sets it has played. It ranks last in the conference in most important stat categories, from total kills to aces to blocks. However, despite this lack of competitiveness, Northwestern’s postseason goals aren’t dead just yet. The top 15 Big Ten finishers advance to the postseason conference tournament, and anything can happen from there in a single-elimination format. The ‘Cats have seven games remaining on their schedule, and likely must win four of them to avoid the conference’s bottom three. Let’s break down what NU needs to do in its remaining games. Must win: 2/2 Saturday versus Rutgers Rutgers is 10-12 on the year and 1-9 in the Big Ten. Its lone conference win is a sweep over Ohio State, but it has lost in three or four sets in its other nine games. The Scarlet Knights struggle with defense and lack options on the offensive end, representing a winnable game for the ‘Cats. NU will walk onto its home floor on Halloween night desperate for a win over Rutgers; if Northwestern can’t muster up some evil spirits and come away with this one, then it might not win a Big Ten game all year. Nov. 12 versus Iowa Iowa is 13-11 on the year and 2-8 in Big Ten play. The Hawkeyes beat Rutgers in three sets earlier in the season and just pulled off a surprising upset over a UCLA team that has been a top-third team in the conference. Iowa’s dynamic hitters sparked the upset, but its season has been defined more by lackluster serve receive and defense. The Hawkeyes are an up-and-down team capable of playing with the best, so the ‘Cats will need to bring a balanced consistency to knock off the black and gold. Winnable: 2/3 Thursday at Illinois Illinois is 14-7 overall and 6-4 in conference play. Matt Campbell addressed this, and other question in his weekly press conference. On season goals Two questions revolved around expectations and goals, and the theme in both answers around improving the team one week at a time. It’s not “1-0,” but it’s pretty close. Campbell said his experience helps. He said he rebuilt Iowa State’s program three times, and he rebuilt Toledo’s when he took over. He said leadership means building culture and finding why results are missing. It does not mean leaving the plan or the standards. He admitted the frustration and disappointment, the same as fans feel. He said his mission is sustained success over a long period. He splits the season into four quarters, and the team now enters the third. His first goal is the identity of the program: who it wants to be. He said the staff has focused on leadership and identity, not on wins, losses, or end goals. He said results follow when those things are right. He did not mention a bowl game. item.title: Spurs super sub Keldon Johnson hasn't let gash inside his mouth slow him down
item.description: October 26, 2026, San Antonio, TX: San Antonio Spurs guard Keldon Johnson talks to children during a RBFCU Spurs Youth Basketball League clinic at CentroMed Health & Wellness Clinic in San Antonio, Texas Monday, October 26, 2026. (Photo by Reginald Thomas II/San Antonio Spurs) (Reginald Thomas II/ San Antonio Spurs) Keldon Johnson's season-high 14 points in the Spurs' 130-103 dismantling of Sacramento came a week after he suffered a deep cut on the inside of his right cheek that required three stitches to close. The 2026 NBA Sixth Man of the Year suffered the painful gash in a collision with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander in the season-opening loss to Oklahoma City. "It was pretty painful, but we made it work," Johnson said. "The Spurs doctors took care of me, got me some smoothies and stuff like that to make sure I can eat." item.title: Davies crossing divide between pitch and boardroom
item.description: Ben Davies was one of eight new FAW Council appointments in August [BBC Sport] Inside the committee room, surrounded by suits and the formal quiet of administrative procedure, Ben Davies looks surprisingly comfortable. For over a decade, the Wales and Tottenham Hotspur defender's natural domain has been the high-stakes intensity of Premier League and international football. But in a week when the Football Association of Wales (FAW) is convening to shape the nation's footballing future, Davies is occupying a very different seat at the table. Appointed to the FAW Council in August 2026 as a dedicated representative for Welsh players, the Wales captain hopes to bridge the gap between those who execute the strategy on the pitch and those who draft it in the boardroom. BBC Wales Sport was granted rare access to the FAW council's inner workings at Dragon Park in Newport, where Davies joined fellow executives to discuss the future of Welsh football. The 33-year-old's decision to take on administrative responsibilities alongside a demanding playing schedule comes down to a simple impulse - stewardship. "Firstly, it's an absolute honour and privilege to play football for Wales," he said. "Because of that honour and how much I've loved doing it - and still love doing it - you want to give back in any way you can. "If I can help using my stature and position as a player to help Welsh football, I'm more than happy to do that." FAW sets ambitious 10-year plan but seeks more money FAW boss renews call for Infantino to step down A player's perspective at the table Looking around the room, there is the usual entourage of older men in suits. But it's also clear the FAW has undergone a significant structural change in recent years, modernising its model to bring broader expertise to its decision-making. A notable contingent of women and people of previously underrepresented ethnic backgrounds were also present at the meeting. That's not to say that having the more seasoned administrators there is a bad thing. After all, they bring decades of operational knowledge, but having different voices - including Davies' - and direct experience of modern football is a welcome sight. Davies, a Europa League winner and Champions League runner-up with Spurs, acknowledges that dynamic with characteristic modesty, while identifying precisely what he brings to the discussion. "There are a lot of people in that room with a lot of experience that know a lot about what goes on behind the scenes in football," he conceded. "[They] probably know a lot more than I do. I've only been a player. But ultimately, I'm here with a player's voice. "Having played at the highest level for a long time, I want to be able to maintain those standards, bring us up to the levels that I've seen in the world of football, maintain us, and put us in a good place going forward." item.title: “Would Be Like LeBron James Or Tom Brady Not Playing 4th Quarter” – Mets Legend Weighs In On Free Agent Pitchers Amid NY’s Interest In Tarik Skubal
item.description: Tarik Skubal - LA Dodgers | © Imagn The biggest question for the New York Mets this offseason is how aggressively the front office will pursue impending free agent Tarik Skubal. The two-time reigning Cy Young winner is expected to sign the biggest pitching contract in MLB history, potentially surpassing Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s 12-year, $325 million deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers. On “The Mets Pod,” Ron Darling, a member of the Mets team that won the 1986 World Series, compared today’s MLB starting pitchers to legendary players in other sports, including seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady and four-time NBA champion LeBron James. “The problem you have is that these great players who you are going to pay a lot of money only pitch two-thirds of the game, and that’s on the high end, not on the low end,” Darling said. “The most you’re going to get is two-thirds of the game. It would be like LeBron and Tom Brady not playing the fourth quarter. So how valuable is that? How far do you go? Is it the difference maker that you think it is? Because you still have to get nine outs.” Darling seemed to imply that no team needs to go all-out on Skubal in the offseason. Tarik Skubal In Line For Two Big Offseason Records According to MLB.com’s Mark Feinsand, Tarik Skubal is expected to not only surpass Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s $325 million deal but also break another offseason record held by two former Cy Young winners. Justin Verlander and Max Scherzer hold the record for highest average annual value ($43.33 million). Feinsand thinks Skubal could surpass that number. “The record for largest guaranteed contract ever given to a pitcher is Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s 12-year, $325 million deal with the Dodgers, while Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander share the record for highest average annual value ($43.33 million). Based on conversations with executives and agents around the league, Skubal’s next deal could exceed both,” Feinsand wrote on MLB.com. The Dodgers and the Mets are expected to pursue Skubal in the offseason. Other teams are also in the mix, including the New York Yankees and the San Francisco Giants. item.title: Three Former Red Sox Had Major Hand In Brewers Game 4 Loss
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Shane Drohan The Milwaukee Brewers had a chance to sweep the Tampa Bay Rays in the World Series, but failed to do so. At the forefront of it all were three former Boston Red Sox players. It was a bullpen game for the Brewers, and Dustin May took the mound first for them. May was acquired by the Red Sox last year in exchange for James Tibbs III, but he was not great for them. He was solid for the St. Louis Cardinals this year, and the Brewers went and got him at the trade deadline. He went three innings in Game 4, giving up two earned runs. May gave up a leadoff single in the fourth that came around to score and give the Rays a 2-1 lead. However, how that run came around to score also involved a former Red Sox player. David Hamilton fielded a ground ball with one out and May's runner, who got to second on a groundout previously, was trying to get to third. Hamilton tried to tag him, missed and then fired an off-target throw to first base that allowed the runner to score. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! To be fair, Hamilton made up for his error by hitting a solo home run in the top of the fifth inning to tie the game back up. After that, there were no runs scored and barely any base runners until the 12th inning. In the top of the 12th inning, Cooper Pratt hit a home run that looked to be the decisive blow and would make him a legend in Milwaukee at just 22 years old. The only problem was that the Brewers had used most of their arms and had very few options for the 12th inning. They turned to Shane Drohan, another former Red Sox player, who came to Milwaukee with Hamilton in the Caleb Durbin trade. Drohan inherited a runner after an error in the 12th and had to get three outs to win the World Series. Instead, he gave up four consecutive hits and the Brewers lost. A new report from the Philadelphia Inquirer says that a well-connected source inside the NFL said the league is “furious” with the Eagles over how they have handled the Hurts situation. The shield is in the optics business, and when one of the league’s most well-known players is mishandled, especially when it comes to player health, they’re going to be angry with anyone involved in the situation. An NFL/NFLPA joint investigation is currently ongoing into the Eagles’ conduct, which will try to determine what role, if any, the organization had in either exacerbating Hurts’ injury, leading to the end of his season, or if they knowingly misled the league on the severity of Hurts’ injury. Today we dive into what makes this whole situation tick, and establish a timeline of what went on with Jalen Hurts. Sunday, October 4 The Eagles lose to the Rams 24-20. Jalen Hurts was cleated in the calf at some point during the game, which is when a player (teammate or opponent) steps or stomps with their cleats. There is no indication he made medical staff aware of the injury either when it occurred, or immediately following the game. Monday, October 5 to Wednesday, October 7 Hurts resumes his typical training and practice protocol. The Eagles claim that Hurts again did not make them aware of any injury. Thursday, October 8 Jalen Hurts tells the team medical staff that he is having discomfort in his calf. He continues to practice throughout the session. For the first time he is added to the team injury report , which shows him practicing Wednesday, Thursday, and then listed as a “Full Participant” for Friday. His game status is noted as “Unspecified.” Saturday, October 10 The Eagles leave Philadelphia to fly to London for their game against the Jaguars. Hurts is on the flight, and all indications are that he will play. After landing, the team sends Hurts to receive imaging, with an ultrasound showing “small superficial blood clots” in the calf he was experiencing pain in. Hurts is admitted to the hospital for monitoring, where he stays overnight — but is told not to sleep, which could increase the risk of the clots becoming more serious .

item.title: Detroit Lions' DJ Wonnum named Player of the Week after blocked FG
item.description: Detroit Lions defensive end DJ Wonnum was named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week on Wednesday, Oct. 28, after he blocked a late field goal in the Lions' win over the Green Bay Packers. Wonnum got two fingers on a 35-yard field goal try by Trey Smack four plays after the Packers stopped the Lions on fourth-and-1 from their own 24-yard line in a tie game late in the fourth quarter. The Lions followed Wonnum's block with a 10-play drive that ended in Jake Bates' game-winning field goal as time expired, and several players said after they game they didn't even realize Wonnum tipped the ball. "Did he block it?" Lions quarterback Jared Goff said after the game. "Amazing, yeah, I didn’t know he blocked it. That’s awesome. That’s a huge individual effort. The field goals from there typically are pretty high percentage, and to be able to get the ball back − to miss that fourth down conversion and get the ball back with no harm, no foul, again hat’s off to our defense and DJ there with the block." Wonnum, who's tied for the team lead with five sacks, is the second Lions player to win a player of the week award this season. Jahmyr Gibbs was named NFC Offensive Player of the Week after he ran for 151 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions' Week 5 win over the Arizona Cardinals. item.description: John Mersits/Cal Sport Media/Newscom/The Mega Agency; ZUMAPRESS.com / MEGA Ex- New York Yankees player Joba Chamberlain has reacted after fellow former teammate Jorge Posada said he no longer feels the love from his team. Appearing on New York Post Sports’ The Show on Tuesday, October 27, Posada, 55, was asked whether he would take a position with the team now, perhaps as a member of the coaching staff. “I could, but I don’t think they want me there to tell you the truth. I don’t feel welcome when I go there, you know?” the catcher, who played 17 years for the Yankees, responded. “Even in spring training, I don’t feel like — I’m just like, I don’t know, like, I don’t feel welcome. My last season of my career was a really tough one when it comes to handling everything in my part and also the Yankees toward Jorge Posada. So, it’s tough to go back and feel that again,” he added. As he admitted, his final season in 2011 wasn’t an easy one. He, at one point, asked to be taken off the lineup after being moved to designated hitter and backup first baseman. item.title: NFL’s first Paris game faces backlash over changed French anthem lyrics
item.description: Source: bellafotosolo/Depositphotos The NFL’s first regular-season game in France drew controversy before kickoff on October 25, 2026, when singer Nina Tonji changed a word in the French national anthem. Her performance at Stade de France prompted criticism across French social media. Tonji replaced a familiar phrase in La Marseillaise, raising questions about the anthem’s historical meaning and whether performers should alter national symbols. The dispute became a separate story from the Pittsburgh Steelers’ 16-10 victory over the New Orleans Saints. A historic NFL game opens with controversy The NFL brought regular-season competition to France for the first time, with Pittsburgh facing New Orleans at Stade de France in Saint-Denis, outside Paris. The game attracted 78,488 spectators to the country’s national stadium. Before the teams began playing, Franco-Canadian singer Nina Tonji performed France’s national anthem. The ceremony introduced a historic event in the league’s international expansion, with American football taking center stage before a French audience. Although Tonji received applause inside the stadium, criticism followed when recordings circulated online. French media outlets highlighted a lyrical difference that prompted viewers to question her interpretation of the country’s best-known patriotic song. One changed word sparks widespread criticism The controversy centered on Tonji replacing “impur,” meaning “impure,” with “uni,” meaning “united,” in the anthem’s familiar refrain. That substitution changed the wording of a passage closely associated with France’s revolutionary history. The traditional phrase is “Qu’un sang impur abreuve nos sillons!” Tonji instead sang “Qu’un sang uni abreuve nos sillons!” The alteration changed the meaning while preserving the surrounding words and musical arrangement. French outlets, including Le Parisien and RTL, reported the reaction on October 26. Videos circulated on social media, drawing complaints from viewers who believed the anthem should retain its established wording during public ceremonies. Why the original French lyrics matter La Marseillaise dates to April 1792, when France entered a conflict with Austria during the French Revolution. Claude-Joseph Rouget de Lisle composed the song in Strasbourg for the Army of the Rhine. The phrase “sang impur” belongs to the anthem’s wartime language. It is commonly understood as referring to France’s enemies, while the surrounding lyrics urge citizens to defend their country against approaching hostile forces. Replacing “impure” with “united” changes that historical meaning. Some critics argued that the revised passage becomes confusing because it retains the image of blood watering French fields without clearly identifying an opposing force. item.title: Wisconsin basketball not taking unneeded risk with Will Garlock injury
item.description: MADISON – Wisconsin men’s basketball has a 2026-27 roster that Greg Gard believes is “as big as we’ve been in a long time.” “If you watch the trends in college basketball right now, big is back, so to speak,” Gard said at the Badgers ’ Oct. 6 local media day . Gard had less of that size to work with in the Badgers’ 82-65 exhibition win over Oklahoma State , as 7-foot forward Will Garlock was sidelined with an injury. Garlock suffered the injury in practice and is considered day-to-day, according to UW sports information. He was not in uniform and did not participate in pregame warmups at the Kohl Center. Gard gave a few more details about the Middleton native’s recovery in his postgame news conference. “He’s going to go through some more testing tomorrow and be evaluated more,” Gard said. “At this point in time in the season, we’re not going to put anybody in a risk. We’ll figure out what’s exactly going on and then go from there.” Gard described Garlock at the Big Ten’s annual basketball media day as “maybe our most improved player.” He has frequently stood out in practices that were open to the media in the summer and again in the preseason. That follows a freshman season averaging 1.1 points and 1.1 rebounds in 6.8 minutes per game. Wisconsin has started Nolan Winter and Victory Onuetu in the frontcourt in all three exhibitions. Rapp and Garlock played significant roles off the bench when they were healthy enough to play. Rapp missed most of the offseason with a knee injury and did not play against UW-Parkside.
